newsitem.title: UK: UK fund managers' enthusiasm for UK shares wanes.
newsitem.headline: UK fund managers' enthusiasm for UK shares wanes.

text.p: The number of UK-based fund managers who were bullish on the UK economy and stock market continued to dwindle last month, according to a Merrill Lynch Gallup Survey published on Monday.
The survey, which polled 67 institutions managing $1,470 billion, showed sellers of UK stocks outnumbered buyers by seven percent. That's up from five percent in the previous month.
Fund managers were polled between March 3 and March 5.
The strength in sterling, which could adversely affect UK exports and corporate earnings, probably led to the decline in optimism, Merrill Lynch said.
Earnings per share growth is forecast to be 8.6 percent, down from 10 percent last October, the survey said.
The latest results showed that 70 percent of managers expected an improvement in the UK economy, down from a peak of 91 percent last July.

A growing number of managers, 57 percent, believed the EMU will take place, but the start date will be delayed. Only three percent predicted the UK will participate in the first round of monetary union.
Asked which equity market they favoured within Continental Europe, a 35 percent majority said they preferred the German stock market.
A 52 percent majority said they least liked the Italian equity market. --London newsroom +44 171 542 5106
